summary: A local-interest article on how wearable fitness technology has become mainstream among area runners, gym-goers and wellness practitioners in the second half of 2023. It describes new devices such as the TitanTrack, PulseGear Pro, NutriWear Clip and ZenBand, and how clubs, gyms and trainers use their data. It also covers concerns about accuracy, privacy and a digital divide, and concludes that local response is mixed but generally positive.
one_line: Local fitness enthusiasts, clubs, gyms and wellness instructors adopt wearable tech in late 2023, while privacy, accuracy and access concerns persist.
key_facts: The TitanTrack and PulseGear Pro were released on September 15 and October 4, 2023, respectively.
The TitanTrack offers step counting, heart rate monitoring and a new hydration tracker that encourages users to meet recommended water intake.
The PulseGear Pro has a stress measurement tool and an integrated program that adapts workouts based on fatigue levels; local fitness guru Emily Torres swears by it.
Emily Torres says the PulseGear Pro is "like having a personal trainer on your wrist."
A local 10k charity race on September 17, 2023 saw nearly everyone wearing wearable tech, including smart shoes like the SwiftStep X5.
The Sprintwell Runners club, whose president is Mark Liu, incorporates wearable data into group challenges and says it has brought members closer.
FitHub re-opened on October 19, 2023 after renovation and gives members a FitHub Band that tracks workout intensity and suggests when to move to the next machine.
FitHub trainer Sandra Bell uses device data on her tablet to tailor clients' fitness plans.
The NutriWear Clip, launched November 1, 2023, clips onto a plate, analyzes a meal's nutritional content and syncs it with the user's activity tracker.
Dietitian Jacob Moreno cautions about the accuracy of the NutriWear Clip's food analysis, saying "Not all calories are created equal."
The ZenBand, released December 8, 2023, offers meditation and mindfulness programs to reduce anxiety and improve sleep quality.
Yoga instructor Cassandra Leigh uses ZenBand in classes at TranquilSpace Studio to measure heart rate variability as an indicator of stress.
Critics raise concerns about data security, over-reliance, accuracy and a digital divide due to cost and technical know-how.
Cyber security expert Darren Scott advises users to read privacy agreements as companies like MegaFit Corp and PulsoTech update their policies.
